value.hook: Open before putting any value into an error's Display, a receipt line or a refusal; before choosing render::line vs caller_text; before testing an atomic write or a race branch; or when pr-freeze says UNSTABLE after a PR body edit
value.title: Caller text vs daemon text, errors render at the source, and proving atomic writes

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Lessons from #193 (F142, four BLOCK rounds) and #199 (F148).

1. Two kinds of text, two renderers.
   - A caller's free text (reasons, whys, notes, subjects, tombstone reasons, recorded paths) is ALWAYS fenced with `render::caller_text`, never shown plain because it "looks safe". Squirrel blocked a blacklist that only checked `[pij from`; frames also come as `[pij bg]`, `[pij role:...` and `[pij output]`.
   - `render::line` is only for the daemon's own words and closed values. It stays plain only as one line with no `[pij ` marker; otherwise it fences.

2. One line-break definition. `render::is_line_break` (LF, CR, VT, FF, NEL, U+2028, U+2029) and `is_one_line` are shared by render, admission and the report one-line rule. `char::is_control` misses U+2028 and U+2029.

3. Make errors safe at the source. `PijError`'s Display renders every seat, reason, record and adapter word it carries, so every `to_string()` consumer is safe without per-caller fixes. The contract test in error.rs is an exhaustive match with no wildcard (`hostile`), so a new variant fails to compile until it is listed. One gap: a variant handled there but left out of `samples` still passes.

4. Sweeps get audited. Any inventory row marked "safe" (owner-only bg jobs, delivered notes from the repo, `render_state` showing the caller's own card) was traced and found false: parents tail children, notes carry stored holding fields, and `pij state <id>` reads other seats. Before marking a field safe, trace who else can read it.

5. Prove an atomic write deterministically. Hold the old file open, write, then read the held handle: a rename leaves it unchanged, while an in-place write changes it. An empty status file means "no exit yet", not malformed (F148).

6. When an HTTP test can't reach a race branch (for example an earlier live-seat check refuses first), say so in the PR. Cover the branch with a unit test of the shared code, and record the surviving HTTP mutant honestly. Reviewers accepted that.

7. CI: editing a PR body starts a second `delivers` run and cancels the first. pr-freeze then reads UNSTABLE; run `gh run rerun <cancelled id>`, then freeze again.

8. Answer role requests with `pij send <pm> --in-reply-to <request id>`; that stops the limit clock.
